results.name: IBM Products Multiple Vulnerabilities
results.description:
Multiple vulnerabilities have been identified in the multiple IBM products, leading to XSS, information disclosure, and spoofing attacks.

How it can be Exploited
CVE-2022-22365: IBM WebSphere Application Server, with the Ajax Proxy Web Application (AjaxProxy.war) deployed, is vulnerable to spoofing.

CVE-2021-39043: The cross-site scripting vulnerability exists in IBM Jazz Team Server which could allow hackers to embed arbitrary JavaScript code in the Web UI.

CVE-2020-4970: The information disclosure vulnerability exists in IBM Security Identity Governance and Intelligence because failure occurs while properly enabling HTTP Strict Transport Security.

results.name: Charming Kitten Hackers Impersonate Journalist in Phishing Attacks
results.description:
A hacker group linked with the Iranian government attempted to steal email login information from their targets through fake interview requests and impersonating a New York Times journalist.

Aimed at journalists, activists, people in academia, and prominent Iranians living outside the country, the phishing attacks are the work of Charming Kitten, also known as Phosphorus,  APT35, or Ajax Security Team.

results.name: Magic Hound Campaign Attacks Saudi Targets
results.description: Unit 42 has discovered a persistent attack campaign operating primarily in the Middle East dating back to at least mid-2016 which we have named Magic Hound. This appears to be an attack campaign focused on espionage. Based upon our visibility it has primarily targeted organizations in the energy, government, and technology sectors that are either in in or business interests in Saudi Arabia. The adversaries appear to have evolved their tactics and techniques throughout the tracked time-period, iterating through a diverse toolset across different waves of attacks. Link analysis of infrastructure and tools also revealed a potential relationship between Magic Hound and the adversary group called “Rocket Kitten” (AKA Operation Saffron Rose, Ajax Security Team, Operation Woolen-Goldfish) as well as an older attack campaign called Newscasters.
